questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
International Hub
Cheap living costs
Interesting City/Place
University Conditions

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: HKU is very good witht their communication however there are a lot of information given and forms to be filled.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Nothing

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: They give necessary information, but regarding choosing courses and social introduction it is very limited. It is help to self-help.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
I lived on-campus but I lived from on another campus than the one I studied at. 
HKU offers student dorms.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: The kitchen is very limited and cramped. I used the microwave but they have a very little stove, be aware that you have to use and store your pantries yourself.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It can be a little bit rough in the beginning, small space, limited area to relax and socialize. The locals may seem very shy, but if you start talking with them they will answer back. Living on a local student dorm is a cultural experience, some of those are very similar to a "kollegie-fællesskab" in Denmark.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The add-drop period is a little bit stressful, as courses get filled up and scheduling conflicts often happen.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You register before arrival, and then there is an add-drop period, where you try different courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can always send an email, which will be replied to on the same or the following day.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read about the curriculum and exam type. Ask around if anyone knows anything about the course. Maximise on the add-drop period some of the courses are not as you expect.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The courses and exams can be very tough.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses varies a lot. Some of them are very hard, and others are easier to follow. In general, I had the impression that the courses offered by the math department were very hard and also the statistical department. Business and arts/humanities departments were easier

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I did not particularly like the teaching. The lectures were, as always, of varying quaility. Some of the lectures I had were very good others not as much. However tutorials are non-existing or of no use. The tutorials is a race to show what has to be shown with no emphasis on learning

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Algebra 1
Introduction to Optimization
Financial Economics 1
Statistical Machine Learning
Natural Language Processing

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Natural Language Processing from the linguistics department is a reasonable course that gives you room to breathe. 
Statistical Machine Learning is a well-planned course which only requires a mathematical intuition and touches upon a lot of different topics.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food is expensive because you have to eat out almost every day. 
Everything in Hong Kong is a little bit expensive. 
Transport prices are reasonable, and travel prices are reasonable.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are sports clubs available but they are almost closed off for internationals. The university is not focused upon social activities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Rowing clubs

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: KEYS. A christian organziation which puts you in contact with locals where you can go out and eat. Midnight Runners.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Travel around. Singapore, Malaysia, Mainland China especially. All around south east asia is cool.
Visit Korea and Japan in the beginning as it gets colder.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. Hong Kong is bustling and open for internationals.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They are very shy, but I met some nice people.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Respect, Acadmic striving and the order.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be aware of the difficulty and workload associated with the courses.
Say yes to everything the first month.
Email the faculty or department they reply very fast

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Use the exam base to see past exams. Feed it into AI to see how hard the past papers actually are.
Apply for housing in Jockey Club 3, but don't stress if you don't get it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making new friends, being a little bit uncomfortable and scared at first, and being academically challenged beyond imagination

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adjusting to the housing and making new friends in the beginning.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy the ride, the first month is tough but do not take anything for granted it is over before you know it.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
